$comment: Advisories that are known, assessed and deliberately still here. Read by scripts/check-advisories.mjs.
An entry is a dated decision, not a suppression: when recheckAfter passes, the gate fails until
a human looks again. Deleting an entry whose advisory is gone is required, not optional, because
an acceptance that matches nothing reads as a live risk assessment.
The full reasoning for each entry lives in docs/security-notes.md. Keep the two in step.

accepted.reason: Bundled inside aws-cdk-lib, which names minimatch in bundleDependencies, so npm never re-resolves it and an overrides entry cannot reach it. Measured 2026-08-04, with the repeat recipe in docs/security-notes.md: adding the override left the nested copy at 5.0.8, and npm audit fix declines it in its own words as a bundled dependency that cannot be fixed automatically. Re-checked 2026-08-16 during the scanner head-to-head fixes: the cooldown had opened for aws-cdk-lib 2.264.0 (published 2026-08-10), it was installed in a worktree, and its bundled copy is still brace-expansion 5.0.8 with npm audit unchanged, so the lockfile was restored rather than bumped for nothing. The newest release, 2.265.0 (published 2026-08-13T19:54Z), leaves the three-day cooldown at 2026-08-16T19:54Z and has not been inspected; whether its bundle moved to 5.0.9 is unknown until it is installed and read. Reachable only at synthesis time on a developer machine or in CI, never in Lambda and never in the request path, over glob patterns this repository wrote itself.
